newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says ties with Singapore back to normal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says ties with Singapore back to normal.

text.p: Two outspoken Malaysian leaders said on Thursday relations between Malaysia and Singapore were back on track after ties had plunged to their lowest point in years.
Minister of International Trade and Industry Rafidah Aziz told a news conference in Malaysia's southern city of Johor Baru that ties were back to normal, the national news agency Bernama reported.
"We are happy to extend co-operation," Rafidah said after meeting Singaporean officials to discuss a "growth triangle" involving southern Malaysia, northern Indonesia and Singapore.
"Singapore and Malaysia have been such close neighbours," she added.
Johor chief minister Abdul Ghani Othman, also at the news conference, said: "There is no problem with the relationship."
But it was little more than a month ago that Rafidah and Abdul Ghani were sharply critical of Singapore over remarks about Johor by Singapore's former prime minister and elder statesman Lee Kuan Yew.

In a court affidavit made in a libel suit against an opposition politician, Lee described Johor Baru as a city "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings". Malaysia reacted to what it perceived as a major insult with fury. Lee, in a rare move, offered an unreserved apology, and when Kuala Lumpur still seethed, asked the court to have the remarks stricken from the record.

One of the most outspoken Malaysian leaders during the row with Singapore was in the island republic on Thursday offering an olive branch. The chairman of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's United Ahmad Zahid Hamidi Malays National Organisation (UMNO) met Information Minister George Yeo.
Ahmad Zahid told reporters after the meeting that the
acrimony and bad blood that marked the row between the neighbours was slowly dissipating.
"When the time comes and the book is really closed (on the dispute), we can work hand in hand," he said.

Yeo said the two sides should maintain lines of communication. "If we don't talk, things can get worse than they need to be," Yeo said. Ahmad Zahid led an extraordinary demonstration in Johor Baru after Lee's remarks were publicised in Malaysian newspapers in March. The UMNO youth protesters shouted slogans and waved placards calling Lee "senile" and "ignorant".

The two nations are closely entwined by history, culture and business. They were united in the Malaysian Federation between 1963 and 1965 when Malaysia booted out its southern neighbour over basic policy differences.
